To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) In the compactified HEIDI model the Higgs sector is composed of two doublets, one of which is a Standard Model-like Higgs doublet, and the other of which is an inert Higgs doublet that does not couple to fermions and is responsible for dark matter.

the compactified model has the same phenomenological properties as the higher-dimensional version and that the LHC can discover or exclude the model at the 95% confidence level in the parameter space compatible with precision electroweak constraints.
(i) a Higgs sector with two doublets and two triplets is compatible with all electroweak constraints and (ii) this model can be probed in the golden channel at the Lhc.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: What are the phenomenological implications for the compactified HEIDI model at the LHC? Can the HEIDI model be tested at the LHC and what is its potential? How can one distinguish between the HEIDI model and the Standard Model?
the question whether the Higgs sector of a model can be discovered at the LHC or whether the Higgs boson decays into invisible particles.

the following questions: (i) How does the LHC search for a Higgs-like particle in the golden four-lepton channel change in a model with a compactified higher-dimensional setup? (ii) What is the phenomenological signature of a compactified higher dimensional model in the golden four lepton channel?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the compactified HEIDI model is not excluded by the data, and that the LHC can discover the model at a 5σ level if the Higgs mass is in the range 115 GeV < mH < 130 GeV.

the LHC is able to discover the compactified HEIDI model in the four-lepton channel if the mass of the Higgs boson is below about 150 GeV and if the mass difference between the Higgs bosons is above about 20 GeV.

, in this model class, the Higgs sector is either very light and thus not accessible at the LHC, or it is very heavy and decays predominantly into gauge boson pairs, or the Higgs sector has masses in the range between 100 GeV and 200 GeV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the compactified HEIDI model can explain all the observed deviations in the electroweak sector and the Higgs sector, while at the same time providing a viable dark matter candidate.
the compactified model is a very good alternative to the Standard Model in explaining the Higgs-like signal observed at the LHC.
the compactified models are in general more challenging for discovery at the LHC, but that the models are still discoverable for a large region of their parameter space.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LHC can discover the new scalars in the HEIDI models in the golden channel.
, in contrast to previous studies, a large part of the allowed parameter space can be explored with the current data and, with more data, the full parameter space can be probed.

the compactification mechanism can lead to a suppression of the Higgs signal strength in a way which is compatible with the current data and can be probed at the LHC with 300/fb of integrated luminosity.
